newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends weak on bourse jitters.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends weak on bourse jitters.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker across the board on Wednesday on jitters and speculation triggered by a continuing slump in share prices on the local bourse, traders said.
"Dealers became very nervous over the bourse...which has accrued sharp losses this week," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both ended 1.7 centavos weaker, at 7.9290/7.9310 and 7.9230/7.9280 per dollar, respectively.
The IPC index of Mexican shares was down 0.64 percent at 3,690.56 points as foreign exchange markets were closing.
The Dow Jones was meanwhile down 0.62 percent at 6,569.88 points.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed 1.5 centavos weaker at 7.9150/7.9180 per dollar.
"Local interest rates and the bourse had reacted to recent increases in U.S. interest rates, so now it was the peso's turn to suffer," another trader said.
Dealers said dollars may have been in demand from traders hedging against a possible rise in U.S. long bond yields in response to Friday's publication of U.S. nonfarm payrolls data.
Bellwether 27-day Cetes gained 127 basis points to 21.86 percent at Banco de Mxico's Tuesday evening primary auction.
U.S. 30-year Treasury bonds were down 2/32 to yield 7.08 percent at midafternoon trade.
"Some foreign dealers bought dollars, but in general I feel the peso weakened due more to speculation than a real outflow of foreign capital," a dealer said.
